title: Oscar and the Debt
premise: Marguerite Delacroix, a crash investigator haunted by the deaths of his family in row twelve of a flight no one will explain, is pulled into a case where a passenger jet's records vanish mid-flight while it is still airborne. Following the ghost flight leads him to a hidden network that erases disasters before they happen, trading lives for geopolitical stability. To expose them, he must extract Elena Vasquez, a defector who may be deliberate bait dangled ahead of a global summit where the network plans its largest erasure yet. Marguerite sacrifices his anonymity and nearly his life to force the truth into the open at the summit, winning justice outside the law but losing the invisibility that once kept him safe.
about_author: August Thornbury is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reviewing accident reports before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Opening on the anniversary of his family's crash, Marguerite works a routine investigation in Lisbon, methodical and emotionally sealed off. A colleague notes he only takes cases 'no one wants attributed.' Emotional beat: grief worn as professional armor.

chapters.title: The Ghost Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. He's handed an anomaly: Flight 4471's digital records vanished while the plane was still in the air, though it landed safely. Passengers deplaned into unmarked vehicles. Beat: first crack in his controlled world—curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: Passengers Without Shadows
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. He interviews a listed passenger's family and finds the man never existed—or was erased so thoroughly even his wife doubts her memories. Beat: dread; the erasure is personal, not bureaucratic error.

chapters.title: The Quiet Man from Geneva
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. A courteous stranger warns him off, offering a promotion and a transfer. Marguerite recognizes the offer as a leash. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Won't Say
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. He recovers a corrupted data fragment suggesting the flight's transponder was spoofed by ground infrastructure. Someone owns the sky. Beat: vertigo—the conspiracy is institutional.

chapters.title: The Defector's Letter
chapters.summary: POV Elena Vasquez introduced. A former network analyst hiding in Tallinn sends an encrypted letter to Marguerite: she knows what happened to row twelve. Beat: hope, dangerous and unwelcome.

chapters.title: Thirteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. He reopens his family's case privately and finds the same spoofing signature. His grief has a fingerprint now. Beat: rage crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Tallinn Rain
chapters.summary: POV Elena. She agrees to meet Marguerite but detects surveillance; she's been bait since she defected. Beat: paranoia and reluctant trust as they finally meet in a sauna district safehouse.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Prevented Disasters
chapters.summary: POV Elena. She reveals the network's logic: they erase flights carrying people whose deaths prevent wars, crashes staged or averted to steer history. Row twelve was a trade. Beat: moral horror—the enemy believes itself righteous.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Elena shows him the ledger; his family's flight appears with a margin note: 'approved, contingency held.' Someone chose, then hesitated. Beat: the wound reopened with precision.

chapters.title: Safehouse Burning
chapters.summary: POV Elena. The safehouse is attacked; they escape through Tallinn's old town as it burns behind them. A network operative dies by Elena's hand. Beat: point of no return—she's burned too now.

chapters.title: The Handler Who Cried
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. They interrogate the dead operative's phone and find his handler: Aldous Wren, a summit security consultant. The summit is the target date. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. His agency suspends him; his apartment is searched; his identity documents begin to fail at borders. The erasure machine turns toward him. Beat: loss of the self he hid inside.

chapters.title: Freight Class to Prague
chapters.summary: POV Elena. The pair travels dark via freight trains and forged papers, growing closer through exhaustion and shared danger. Beat: tenderness blooming in hostile soil.

chapters.title: The Archive Under the Lake
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Elena reveals a physical backup archive in a decommissioned Czech reservoir facility—the network's one vulnerability. Beat: a plan forms; hope with a body count attached.

chapters.title: Wren's Dinner Party
chapters.summary: POV Wren (antagonist POV). At a Geneva dinner, Wren calmly justifies the coming summit operation to a skeptical patron. Beat: chilling elegance; the reader sees the enemy's humanity and rejects it.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: POV Elena. Intercepted traffic reveals the network let Elena defect deliberately—to lure whoever inherited row twelve's questions. Marguerite is the real target. Beat: betrayal of their own plan; trust tested.

chapters.title: The Argument in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Elena offers to turn herself in to buy him out. He refuses; they fight, then reconcile over the truth: neither can go back. Beat: commitment forged in conflict.

chapters.title: Prague Dead Drop
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. A contact inside the summit's security staff passes them floor plans and Wren's schedule—for a price Marguerite can't yet pay. Beat: debts accruing; foreshadowing sacrifice.

chapters.title: Halfway to the Summit
chapters.summary: POV Elena. Midpoint: they reach Vienna, archive key in hand, but Elena's extraction route closes when her old handler resurfaces alive. Beat: rising dread—the net tightening.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Erased
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Her handler, Kovac, claims he also wants out and offers the archive's final cipher. Marguerite doesn't trust him; Elena does. Beat: divided loyalties.

chapters.title: Reservoir Night
chapters.summary: POV Elena. Infiltration of the lake archive succeeds until Kovac locks the vault behind them—he sold them out. Beat: trap sprung; lowest tactical ebb.

chapters.title: Water Rising
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Flooded corridors, drowning tension; Marguerite saves Elena using the maintenance knowledge from his crash-investigation years. They escape with partial copies. Beat: survival earned, not given.

chapters.title: What the Copies Show
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The partial archive confirms the summit op: a full-spectrum erasure of a passenger summit delegation, blamed on a hijacking. Beat: stakes made concrete—a massacre disguised as tragedy.

chapters.title: Kovac's Price
chapters.summary: POV Elena. Kovac contacts them: he'll give the cipher and testify if they extract his daughter from a network school in Zurich. Beat: the price of allies; moral complexity deepens.

chapters.title: The School on the Hill
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Extraction of the girl goes almost perfectly—too perfectly. Wren let it happen to tag their route. Beat: pyrrhic victory; surveillance closing in.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: POV Elena. With two days to the summit, they have the cipher, the testimony, and no way in. Marguerite proposes the unthinkable: walk in through the front, as invited press. Beat: audacity born of desperation.

chapters.title: Press Credentials for a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Using erased identities from the archive, Marguerite fabricates a journalist persona—the network's own weapon turned inward. Beat: ironic triumph, fragile as glass.

chapters.title: Wren Knows
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren identifies Marguerite at the summit check-in but lets him enter, preferring to break him publicly. Beat: cat-and-mouse inverted; dread of the gilded cage.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Inside the secured venue, Marguerite locates the broadcast control room while delegations mingle above. Beat: coiled tension; everything poised.

chapters.title: Elena in the Lion's Den
chapters.summary: POV Elena. Elena delivers Kovac's testimony to a sympathetic delegate, but Wren springs his countermove: evidence framing Elena as the hijack architect. Beat: reversal—the bait snaps shut.

chapters.title: Arrested in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Elena is detained by summit security; Marguerite must choose between broadcasting the archive and saving her. Beat: the theme made flesh—justice versus the person.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. He chooses both: he triggers the archive feed naming every traded flight—including row twelve—then goes for Elena. Beat: climax ignites; the invisible made undeniable.

chapters.title: Corridors of Glass
chapters.summary: POV Elena. As the truth floods screens worldwide, Elena fights free of detention during the chaos, wounded. Beat: adrenaline and clarity; the machine stutters.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Erasure
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Cornered, Wren attempts to purge the servers and stage a false-flag explosion. Marguerite confronts him on the roof. Beat: antagonist's ideology collapses into naked self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Fall
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Wren falls to his death reaching for the purge drive; Marguerite catches neither the man nor fully the justice he wanted. Beat: bitter victory; the law never touches Wren.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: POV Elena. Investigations ignite globally; some nations bury the findings, others act. Elena testifies under protection. Beat: justice outside the law bearing imperfect fruit.

chapters.title: The List That Remains
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Marguerite receives the complete ledger and must decide whether releasing every name serves truth or just more grief. He releases it—all of it. Beat: moral resolution; no clean hands.

chapters.title: A Grave in Full Sunlight
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. He visits his family's graves for the first time in thirteen years, finally able to mourn publicly. Elena waits by the gate. Beat: catharsis; grief allowed at last.

chapters.title: Oscar and the Debt
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Epilogue: Marguerite takes a quiet teaching post, mentoring young investigators, his past now a public record rather than a wound. A new anomaly lands on his desk; he smiles, and opens it. Beat: belonging found; the debt paid forward.
